newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk PM says will decline EU invite as warning.
newsitem.headline: Turk PM says will decline EU invite as warning.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Tuesday said he would decline an invitation to attend a dinner with European Union ministers at December's Dublin summit to warn the EU about its attitude to Turkey.

"They will say 'let's chat with Turkey after the three-day meeting'. Just to warn them about this incorrect behaviour, I will tell them the Deputy Prime Minister (Tansu Ciller) will take part and not me, because of parliament work on the budget," Erbakan said.

Erbakan told deputies from his Welfare Party that the EU must change its attitude towards Turkey. Ankara's relations with the EU have been strained by tensions between Greece and Turkey, which are at odds over Aegean territorial disputes and the divided island of Cyprus.
EU concern about Turkey's human rights record, partly responsible for a European Parliament threat to withhold millions of dollars in aid, has further unsettled relations.
"Behaviour towards Turkey must be changed without fail. Europe plays the same record every time it comes here," Erbakan said.
He said European countries applied double standards when criticising Turkey's human rights record.
Ireland invited Erbakan to the December 14 dinner last week after failing to win agreement for a formal meeting on EU-Turkish relations.
Deputy leader Ciller, a pro-Western secularist and Erbakan's predecessor as prime minister, has attended previous EU summit events.
